children.text: A pilgrim town on the hills east of Manila, home to Antipolo Cathedral, the Philippines' first international shrine. From Pinto Art Museum and Hinulugang Taktak Falls to suman, cashews, and the night view from hilltop restaurants, it's a half-day trip from Manila by LRT.
Antipolo is the capital of Rizal province, set on a hill at the edge of the Sierra Madre mountains east of Manila. It's about

from downtown Manila, but sitting over 200m above sea level, the air is a touch cooler, and at dusk the lights of Metro Manila spread out below to the west. The city's name is said to come from "tipolo," a type of breadfruit tree once common here.
What turned Antipolo into a pilgrimage town is the wooden statue of Our Lady of Peace and Good Voyage. In

, Governor-General Juan Niño de Tabora brought this image over from Acapulco, Mexico aboard a galleon, and after it carried the ship safely through several Pacific crossings, it earned its present name. There's also a legend that the statue kept vanishing from the altar only to be found atop a tipolo tree, so the church was built on that very spot.

During World War II, the statue was hidden safely inside an underground oil drum, and after the war it was enshrined again in a newly built church with a domed roof. The Vatican elevated this church to an international shrine, and on
January 26, 2024

it was formally declared the first international shrine in the Philippines and Southeast Asia. Every year on the night of Holy Thursday, huge crowds join the "Alay Lakad" pilgrimage, walking overnight from Manila up to Antipolo.

It would be a shame to see only the cathedral and head back. Pinto Art Museum, which sets contemporary art among Spanish-style white buildings and gardens, Hinulugang Taktak, a waterfall park in the heart of the city, and Sumulong Highway, lined with cafes with fine views, make Antipolo well suited to family outings, dates, and photography trips. Traffic aside, it's about as easy a side trip from Manila as you can get.

Beneath the large domed roof, the statue of Our Lady of Peace and Good Voyage stands on the altar. Many Filipinos come here to pray for safety before working abroad or setting off on a long journey, and the cathedral has a space where pilgrims can light votive candles.

A contemporary art museum founded by a neurologist and collector, where paintings and installations by Filipino artists are scattered among whitewashed buildings, stairways, and tropical gardens. The building itself is a photo spot, and there's a small cafe inside.
A protected landscape in the heart of the city about
1.7km
from the cathedral, with a wide waterfall about
high. The name comes from a legend that a noisy bell (taktak) was thrown (hinulog) into the falls.

Suman — glutinous rice steamed in coconut milk and wrapped in leaves — along with sweet mangoes and savory cashews (kasoy), are Antipolo's three great specialties. Try them at the shops around the cathedral and the souvenir center, and pick some up as gifts.

blocks.title: Hilltop view restaurants and night views

children.text: Sumulong Highway and the hills around town have many cafes and restaurants with open views toward Manila. Grab a seat before sunset and watch the scene shift from the glow of dusk to the city's night lights.
A stone church in the mountains that began as a Franciscan mission church in
, about
40 minutes–1 hour
by car from downtown. Its quiet, old-world atmosphere also makes it a popular wedding venue.

A limestone cave on the way to Boso-Boso, visited by many for its spiritual meaning since some of its stalactites are said to resemble the Virgin Mary and saints. Parts of the passage are narrow and dark, so wear comfortable shoes.

blocks.title: A glimpse of car blessings and pilgrim culture

children.text: On weekends, you can see families parking new cars in the space beside the cathedral to receive a priest's blessing with holy water. From this to pilgrims heading home with suman in hand, it's a close-up look at how Filipino Catholic faith is woven into everyday life.

To also see Boso-Boso Old Church and Mystical Cave, it's best to rework the afternoon plan and rent a car. The mountain roads make public transport inconvenient, and visiting both takes about
3–4 hours
The easiest way is to take the LRT-2 east to its terminus, Antipolo station (formerly Masinag). From Recto station it takes about
35–45 minutes
and costs about
. The first train runs around
5 AM
and the last train from Antipolo station around
9 PM
, so check your return time.
Since
March 23, 2026
, on the Department of Transportation's order, LRT-2 fares have been discounted 50% for all passengers, so the Recto–Antipolo trip is about
. It is a temporary measure in force "until further notice," so it could end at any time.
From in front of Antipolo Station, take a jeepney bound for "Antipolo (Simbahan)" to reach downtown near the cathedral in about
20–30 minutes
, for a fare of about
. There are also jeepneys and UV Express vans running directly from Cubao, taking about
1 hour–1 hour 30 minutes
From Makati or Ortigas, take Ortigas Avenue Extension or Marcos Highway up to Sumulong Highway. On a weekday afternoon it takes about
1 hour–1 hour 30 minutes
, with a one-way Grab fare of around
. Weekend afternoons and the May pilgrimage season bring heavy traffic on the roads into town.
Tricycles connect the cathedral, the falls, and the museum. Expect about
for a short ride, and about
for spots inside residential subdivisions like Pinto Art Museum — agree on the fare before you get in.
The relatively dry
November–April
is best for getting around.
December–February
brings cool evening temperatures around
up on the hills, good for sitting on a view restaurant's terrace, and on clear days you can even see the sea beyond Manila.
March–May
is hot at midday but sees little rain.
In Antipolo,
May
is pilgrimage month. Starting with the Alay Lakad during Holy Week and running through the feast of Our Lady on
the first Tuesday of May
, crowds of pilgrims pack the streets around the cathedral, sometimes closing them off — avoid this period if you want a quiet visit. During the rainy season,
June–October
, afternoon showers are frequent, but it's also when Hinulugang Taktak Falls carries the most water.

Since a day trip from Manila is plenty, few travelers stay overnight, but for family gatherings or a relaxing getaway, you can book resort-style hotels and private-pool villas along Sumulong Highway and the hills in town. Expect about
per night, with view rooms costing more. During pilgrimage season the area around the cathedral gets very crowded, so a quieter place on the outskirts is a better choice.

If you're in Antipolo, be sure to try suman. It's glutinous rice steamed with coconut milk and wrapped in leaves, eaten the local way dipped in coconut caramel (latik) or sugar alongside sweet mango. Roasted or sugar-coated cashews and coconut candy also make good gifts. Most restaurants are hilltop view cafes and Filipino home-style eateries, and long-running view cafes like "Cafe Lupe" are popular for pairing a meal with the night view. Expect about
per meal at restaurants near the downtown cathedral, and about
at view restaurants.
Pinto Art Museum and Hinulugang Taktak are closed on Mondays. Plan your visit between Tuesday and Sunday.
Mass is held frequently inside the cathedral. Avoid sleeveless tops or short shorts, and refrain from taking photos during Mass.
Traffic back to Manila is very heavy on weekend afternoons. It's safer to go on a weekday or plan around the last LRT departure time.
Suman spoils within a day or two at room temperature, so buy gift portions right before heading back and refrigerate them quickly.
Pinto Art Museum has lots of stairs and slopes. Wear comfortable shoes, and visit later in the afternoon for softer garden photos.
The Pinto Art Museum is open Tuesday to Sunday,
10 AM–5 PM
, and students pay
. Large bags and backpacks can't be brought in, and flash photography, video recording, and outside food are prohibited in the galleries. Check the latest information on the
official website
Swimming is banned in the Hinulugang Taktak river due to pollution. Use the separate pool inside the park for water play.
LRT-2 accepts reloadable Beep cards or bank card/QR payment, so you can skip the ticket line. It's a good idea to carry small change for the jeepney ride up from Antipolo Station into town.
Combine with Tanay and Baras, home to Daranak Falls, Masungi Georeserve, and Mount Daraitan, for a 2-day, 1-night trip through Rizal province.

During Holy Week's Alay Lakad and the May pilgrimage season, hundreds of thousands of people crowd around the cathedral and roads are closed. If you plan to visit then, check the latest notices from Antipolo City and the cathedral for traffic controls and the event schedule.
Watch for pickpockets around the cathedral and inside jeepneys, and don't walk around with your phone out in your hand.
Sumulong Highway is a winding hill road, unsafe to walk along at night. Use a vehicle to move between view restaurants.
Inside Mystical Cave there are dark, slippery sections, so children and elderly visitors should take care.
After heavy rain in the wet season, the paths around Hinulugang Taktak can get slippery, and the falls park may close temporarily.
